questions.question:
D4 — Which review posture (mode) for this plan? <gstack-qid:plan-ceo-review-mode>
Project/branch/task: main, PLAN.md saved project views, approach B chosen.
ELI10: The mode sets how ambitious I am allowed to be for the rest of the review. Expansion means I pitch the cathedral version and you opt into each piece. Selective means I harden the current scope AND show you a menu of add-ons to cherry-pick. Hold means the scope is final and I only make it bulletproof. Reduction means I cut to the smallest thing that removes the pain. This is an enhancement to an existing task list, which normally points to Selective.
Stakes if we pick wrong: Too ambitious and a two-week pilot ships late; too narrow and the pilot measures a feature that misses obvious wins like shared team views or a default view.
Recommendation: SELECTIVE EXPANSION because the core is well understood and the interesting choices (shared views, default view, URL links, view sprawl controls) deserve individual yes/no calls rather than a blanket dream or a blanket no.
Note: options differ in kind, not coverage — no completeness score.
A) SELECTIVE EXPANSION (recommended)
  ✅ Current scope gets full rigor first, then each add-on is a separate neutral decision
  ✅ You pick exactly which extras ride along in the pilot
  ❌ More questions during the review than Hold
B) SCOPE EXPANSION
  ✅ Surfaces the 10x version: views as a shareable, linkable platform primitive
  ✅ Enthusiastic recommendations, still opt-in per item
  ❌ Risk of pilot scope ballooning past the two-week window
C) HOLD SCOPE
  ✅ Fastest path to a bulletproof version of exactly what PLAN.md says
  ✅ Zero scope negotiation, maximum rigor on errors, edges, observability
  ❌ Obvious adjacent wins are never surfaced for a decision
D) SCOPE REDUCTION
  ✅ Tests whether URL-persisted filter state alone removes the pain before building save/list/edit/delete
  ✅ Smallest pilot, fastest signal
  ❌ Pilot may measure something too thin to tell whether members actually want saved views
Net: how much of the review is spent on 'make it right' vs. 'make it bigger' vs. 'make it smaller'.

options.label: SELECTIVE EXPANSION (recommended)
options.description: Hold PLAN.md scope as the baseline and harden it, then present each expansion (shared views, default view, URL links, sprawl cap, etc.) as its own neutral yes/defer/skip.

options.label: SCOPE EXPANSION
options.description: Dream big: views as a shareable, linkable primitive. Every expansion pitched enthusiastically, still opt-in one at a time.

options.label: HOLD SCOPE
options.description: Scope is final. Maximum rigor only: architecture, security, error paths, edge cases, observability, rollout. No expansions surfaced.

options.label: SCOPE REDUCTION
options.description: Strip to the minimum that removes the pain, possibly URL-persisted filter state plus a single save action, then review that.

questions.question:
D5 — Expansion 1 of 8: URL-encoded filter state and linkable views? <gstack-qid:plan-ceo-review-expansion-url-state>
Project/branch/task: main, saved project views, EXPANSION mode.
ELI10: Imagine you tweak three filters, hit refresh, and everything is still there. You paste the address to a teammate and they see the same list. That is what putting filter and sort state into the URL gives you, before any save button exists. A saved view then is just a named URL: /projects/42/tasks?view=17, with any unsaved tweaks layered on as query params. Concrete shape: a filter-state serializer/parser shared by the filter bar and the saved-view loader; the view id in the route; unsaved deltas in the query string. Effort: human ~1 day / CC ~20 min.
Stakes if we pick wrong: Without it, back button, refresh, and bookmarks all lose state, and 'reopen a view' means clicking through the picker every time. Many members would never save a view because a bookmark can't do it for them.
Recommendation: A because this is the foundation the other expansions (sharing, default view, deep links from notifications) stand on, and it halves the pain for members who never save anything.
Completeness: A=10/10, B=6/10, C=3/10
A) Add to scope (recommended)
  ✅ Refresh, back button, bookmarks, and pasted links all preserve filters and sort
  ✅ One serializer shared by the filter bar and saved views: DRY by construction
  ❌ Must define a stable, versioned query-param format and test parse/serialize round-trips
B) Defer to TODOS.md
  ✅ Ships the pilot with fewer moving parts in the router
  ✅ Can be added later without changing the saved_views schema
  ❌ Views can't be linked to; pilot measures a weaker experience
C) Skip
  ✅ Zero routing work
  ❌ The 'recreate filters' pain persists for anyone who doesn't save a view
Net: routing work now vs. views that are only reachable through the picker.

options.label: Add to scope (recommended)
options.description: Filter+sort state in the URL, view id in the route, one shared serializer. Human ~1 day / CC ~20 min. Completeness 10/10.

options.label: Defer to TODOS.md
options.description: Ship personal views reachable only via the picker; write URL state up as follow-on work. Completeness 6/10.

options.label: Skip
options.description: Do not pursue URL-encoded filter state. Completeness 3/10.
